questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The function of companion cells is to
options: Provide energy to sieve elements for active transport
Load sucrose into sieve elements by passive transport
Load sucrose into sieve elements by active transport
questions.solution: Companion cells move sugar and amino acids into and out of the sieve elements. In "source" tissue such as the leaf, companion cells use transmembrane proteins to take up sugar and amino acids by active transport. Movement of sugars in the phloem begins at the source, where sugars are loaded (actively transported) into a sieve tube. Loading sets up a water potential gradient that facilitates the movement of sugar.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cork cambium is developed from
questions.solution: Cork cambium (phellogen) is an outermost lateral meristem in woody plants, that develops from permanent tissues in the region of epidermis hypodermis, cortex, and even in outer layers of phloem. It& is also known as a phellogen that forms a layer of cells that produces a secondary protective layer of the stem called the periderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the center (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This type of primary xylem is called
questions.solution: toxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem lies towards the centre. Such an arrangement of primary xylem is called exarch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following tissue is absent in vascular bundles of monocot stem?
questions.solution: Monocot stems& have most of their& vascular bundles& near the outside edge of the& stem. The bundles are surrounded by large parenchyma in the cortex region. There is no pith region in& monocots. In dicot& stems, bundles are present in a ring surrounding parenchyma cells in a pith region.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Viral infection is usually absent in
questions.solution: The apical meristems are present in the apices of primary and secondary shoots and roots of the plant. The cells of apical meristem are in an active stage of division, have dense cytoplasm, thin cell wall, and remain virus-free. Due to this reason, meristematic culture is carried out to obtain virus-free plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a dicotyledonous stem, the sequence of tissues from outside to inside is:
questions.solution: The sequence of tissues from the outside to the inside in a dicotyledonous stem is phellem-phellogen-phelloderm-cortex-endodermis-pericycle-phloem xylem-pith.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are the functions of a medullary ray in plants?

(i) Storage of food
(ii) Secondary growth
(iii) Transmission of water and food
(iv) Seat of origin of inter-fascicular cambium
questions.solution: Medullary or pith rays are essential for the radial conduction of the water, minerals and other organic substances. They transport the substances from center to periphery. These rays are also known as vascular rays or pith rays. They are also the site of origin of inter-fascicular cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mark the correct statement
options: Lenticels pores are larger than stomata.
Lenticular transpiration is only 1% of the total transpiration.
questions.solution: A lenticel is a porous tissue consisting of cells with large intercellular spaces in the periderm of the secondarily thickened organs and the bark of woody stems and roots of dicotyledonous flowering plants. It functions as a pore, providing a pathway for the direct exchange of gases between the internal tissues and atmosphere through the bark, which is otherwise impermeable to gases. Though its contribution is very less in comparison to stomata, it is much needed for the plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following in the order of their location from the periphery to center in the dicotyledons body

I. Endodermis
II.& Metaxylem
III.& Trichoblasts
IV. Phloem
options: IV, I, II, III
IV, II, III,I
I, II, III, IV
III, I, IV, II
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of these cells is trichoblast-endodermis-phloem-metaxylem.

A trichoblast is a cell on the exterior surface of a plant's root that is responsible for forming root hairs. The endodermis is the rod-shaped cells& having the deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of Casparian strips. Phloem and xylem are the vascular bundles present at the center.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following will decay faster?
questions.solution: Sapwood is less durable because it is susceptible to attack by pathogens and insects. It is physiologically active and the conduction of water takes place through it. Heartwood is not attacked by pathogens and insects as it is physiologically inactive. It is filled with tannins, resins, and gums which are not preferred by insects and pathogens.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Closed vascular bundles lack
questions.solution: In closed vascular bundle cambium is absent between xylem and phloem. Ground tissue, conjunctive tissue is pith is present in stele. Stele is the arrangement of V.B. If xylem is outside it is exarch & if xylem is inside or below the phloem it is endarch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The living component of phloem tissue is
questions.solution: Phloem is the complex tissue used in the transport of organic food materials from leaves to stem and roots in a downward direction. It consists of the following elements: Sieve element& (long tube-like cells placed end to end, forming a continuous channel with perforations and hence called sieve tubes), companion cells (thin-walled, more or less elongated cells and which are associated with sieve tubes& with a prominent nucleus and are, therefore, living in nature), phloem parenchyma (elongated with rounded ends and possess cellulosic cell walls and the cells are living and store food reserves in the form of starch and fats), and phloem or bast fibers (elongated lignified sclerenchymatous cells with tapering ends and with simple pits, non-living cells that provide mechanical support to the organs).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is not true about sclereids?
options: These are parenchyma cells with thickened lignified walls.
These are elongated and flexible with tapered ends.
These are commonly found in the shells of nuts and in the pulp of guava, pear, etc.
questions.solution: The sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead sclerenchyma cells with very& narrow cavities (lumen). These are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts; pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota; seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea. Sclerenchyma provides mechanical support to organs. These may be of different types, such as brachysclereids (stone cells) found in grit of pear, apple, macrosclereids (columnar), eg, legume seeds, astrosclereids (star shaped), eg, tea leaves etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If T.S. of young dicot stem is stained with Iodine solution, which of the following region will be stained dark blue?
questions.solution: Iodine solution is used to stain starch. In dicot stem, the innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. The cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains and the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath. Thus staining& gives blue black colour due to starch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the different components from (i) to (iv) in the list given below and tell the correct order of the components with reference to their arrangement from the outer side to the inner side in a woody dicot stem :

(i) Secondary cortex
(ii) Wood
(iii) Secondary phloem
(iv) Phellem
questions.solution: The sequence of different components of woody dicot stem from the outer side to inner side is

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cork cambium results in the formation of cork which becomes impermeable to water due to the accumulation of
questions.solution: Cork is an impermeable buoyant material, the phellem layer of bark tissue that is harvested for commercial use primarily from Quercus suber (the cork oak). Cork is composed of suberin, a hydrophobic substance. Because of its impermeable, buoyant, elastic, and fire retardant properties, it is used in a variety of products, the most common of which is wine stoppers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which type of arrangement is shown by the vascular bundle in the given diagram?
questions.solution: When xylem and phloem within a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii, the arrangement is called radial such as in roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In dicot stem, the xylem is
questions.solution:
There are four types of primary xylem development:& exarch, endarch, centrarch, and mesarch.
In& endarch& development, the protoxylem begins its development from the innermost procambial cells located adjacent to the pith and development progresses outward. Therefore, the protoxylem is found toward the inside and metaxylem toward the outside of the stem. Endarch development is considered the most highly advanced type of primary xylem development.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The meristem that occurs in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axis
questions.solution: primary meristem is called the secondary or lateral meristem. They are cylindrical meristems. Fascicular vascular cambium, interfascicular cambium, and cork-cambium are examples of lateral meristems. These are responsible for producing the secondary tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Annual rings are formed by the activity of
questions.solution: During secondary growth, vascular cambium divides to form secondary xylem which forms wood. The activity of cambium varies in the spring and autumn season. For plants growing in the temperate region, more quantity of light coloured wood is formed in the spring season and less quantity of dark coloured wood is formed in the autumn season. These concentric light and dark coloured wood constitutes an annual ring.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mechanical tissue consisting of living cells is
questions.solution: Collenchyma tissue is made up of elongated cells with irregularly thickened walls. They provide structural support in growing shoots and leaves. They are living cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements pertaining to plant structure is correct?
options: Cork lacks stomata, but lenticels carry out transpiration.
Passage cells help in transfer of food from cortex to phloem.
Sieve tube possess cytoplasm and nuclei.
Shoot apical meristem has a vascular tissue.
questions.solution: Cork is dead tissue that lacks stomata but lenticels present carries transpiration (0.1-1% only) also carries gaseous exchange. Passage cells are present in endodermis which regulates the unidirectional flow of water and minerals in roots. Sieve tube lacks nuclei and the nucleus of the companion cells regulates its functioning. Shoot apex consists of meristematic tissue only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is/are correct statement/s?
options: In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements.
In gymnosperms, tracheids are the chief water transporting elements
The companion cells play an important role in the maintenance of a pressure gradient in the sieve tubes
questions.solution:
Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem. Tracheids are elongated or tube-like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. These are dead and are without protoplasm. The inner layers of the cell walls have thickenings which vary in form. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements. The vessel is a long cylindrical tube-like structure made up of many cells called vessel members, each with lignified walls and a large central cavity.

Companion cells, along with phloem parenchyma play an important role in the maintenance of a pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Companion cells are closely associated with
questions.solution: Sieve tubes are found associated with companion cells of angiosperms. Both sieve tube member and companion cell are derived from the same meristematic cell. Companion cell is nucleated. These cells provide energy for food conduction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.

1. The thread-like cytoplasmic strands, running from one cell to other is known as plasmodesmata.
2. Xylem and phloem constitute the vascular bundle of the stem.
3. The first formed xylem elements are described as metaxylem.
4. Radial vascular bundles are mainly found in the leaves.
options: II is true, but I, III and IV are false
III is true, but I, II and IV are false
IV is true, but I, II and III are false
I and II are true, but III and IV are false
questions.solution: Plasmodesmata are thread-like cytoplasmic strands running from one cell to other and these make connections between adjacent cells. Each vascular bundle is made up necessarily of xylem and phloem elements and the cambium may or may not be present. The first differentiated xylem is called protoxylem, whereas those differentiated afterward are called metaxylem. Radial vascular bundles are mainly found in the roots. In these, there are separate and alternate strands of phloem and xylem present on different radii.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?

$1.$ Conjoint vascular bundles are not present in monocot stem.
$2.$ Casparian strips of endodermis are made of cutin.
$3.$ Pith is large and well developed in monocot roots.
$4.$ Trichome helps in water loss due to transpiration.
questions.solution: Conjoint vascular bundles are present in both monocot and dicot stem. Casparian strips of endodermis are made up of suberin. Trichome helps to reduce water loss by forming a covering and reduces transpiration. Pith is large and well developed in monocots roots and small in dicot root.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The given figure shows T.S. of&
questions.solution: The anatomy of the monocot root& has epidermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles, and pith. As compared to the dicot root which has fewer xylem bundles, there are usually more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles in the monocot root. Pith is large and well developed. Monocotyledonous roots do not undergo any secondary growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following, this kind of vascular bundle can be seen?
questions.solution: A large number of vascular bundles are arranged in a ring; the ‘ring’ arrangement of vascular bundles is a characteristic of dicot stem. Each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The& meristem which occurs in grasses and regenerates parts removed by the grazing herbivores is
questions.solution: The meristem which occurs between mature tissues is known as intercalary meristem. They occur in grasses and regenerate parts removed by the grazing herbivores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
T.S. of a plant material shows the following anatomical features.

I. Vascular bundles are conjoint, scattered and surrounded by sclerenchymatous bundle sheaths.
II. Phloem parenchyma is absent.

What will you identify it as?
questions.solution: In a monocot stem, vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and closed. These vascular bundles are scattered in ground tissue, and each vascular bundls is surrounded by bundle sheath.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Periderm includes
questions.solution: The mechanism in secondary growth in the cortical region of dicot stem involves the process of dedifferentiation.& Few of the cortical cells (in the form of few layers) become meristematic (cork cambium or phellogen) and cut off new cells - cork or phellem (towards the outer side) and phelloderm or secondary cortex (on the inner side). Periderm includes cork or phellem (suberised cell wall), cork cambium or phellogen and secondary cortex or phelloderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pericycle of root produces
questions.solution: Pericycle in root is active in the formation of root branches or lateral roots.& The main function of the pericycle cells is to provide support, structure and protection to the plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vascular bundles where the phloem is found to be present on both sides of xylem is said to be:
questions.solution: The vascular bundle is a long continuous strand of conducting tissues that extend from the roots through the stem and into the leaves. It consists of xylem and phloem that may differ in their arrangement. Bicollateral bundles are those type of vascular bundles in which phloem patches are present on both sides of xylem. These are found in families like Cucurbitaceae, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bulliform cells are found in
options: Grasses - Adaxial epidermal cells of dorsiventral leaves
Grasses - Abaxial epidermal cells of dorsiventral leaves
Grasses - Adaxial epidermal cells of isobilateral leaves
Grasses - Abaxial epidermal cells of isobilateral leaves
questions.solution: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lenticels are formed by rupturing of the epidermis by
questions.solution: In certain regions, the phellogen cuts off closely arranged parenchymatous cells on the outer side instead of cork cells. These parenchymatous cells soon rupture the epidermis, forming lens-shaped openings& called lenticels. Lenticels permit the exchange of gases between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissue of the stem. These occur in most woody trees.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bast fibres are made up of
questions.solution: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. These are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem. These are much elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle-like apices. The cell wall of phloem fibres is quite thick. At maturity, these fibres lose their protoplasm and become dead. Phloem fibres of jute, flax and hemp are used commercially.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Parenchyma is usually present in,

i) Cortex
ii) Phloem fibre
iii) Pericycle
iv) Pith
v) Hypodermis
vi) Medullary rays
vii) Xylem fibres
viii) Mesophyll tissue
questions.solution: Parenchyma is the most abundant tissue commonly known as filling tissue which is present in all plant parts. Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. The hypodermis& is made up of collenchymatous or sclerenchymatous cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The stem with bicollateral vascular bundles and flowers with synandrous condition is found in
questions.solution: In bicollateral vascular bundle, xylem is surrounded on both sides by phloem. In synandrous stamens, both anther lobes and filaments are fused. These conditions are characteristic of the Cucurbitaceae family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fascicular, interfascicular and extra-stelar cambium together constitutes
questions.solution: Lateral meristem is the meristem which occurs on the sides and is helpful in increasing width of stem and root. They divide mainly in one plane (periclinal), increasing the diameter of an organ, e.g., cambium (fascicular and interfascicular cambium), extra stellar cambium, cork cambium and marginal meristem of some leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Root cambium is
questions.solution: The vascular cambium is a meristematic tissue that is responsible for lateral growth and the continued production of new xylem and phloem. In woody roots the vascular cambium (the lateral meristem that gives rise to secondary phloem and secondary xylem) originates from the pericycle and conjunctive tissue. Since it is formed due to dedifferentiation of permanent tissue hence it is secondary meristem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Wood is separated from phloem in dicots by
questions.solution: Vascular cambium is present in between xylem and phloem. Vascular cambium divides to form secondary xylem towards inner side and secondary phloem towards outer side during secondary growth.& The vascular cambium is the main growth tissue in the stems and roots of many plants, particularly in dicots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Collenchyma tissue is characterized by
options: Elongated cells with thickening at the corners
Isodiametric cells with thickening all over the walls
Isodiametric cells with deposits of cellulose and lignin at the corners
Elongated cells which are not involved in the function of food storage
questions.solution: Collenchyma cells are elongated cells with irregularly thick cell walls that provide support and structure.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the layers in a typical monocot root (from the outer surface to the pith)?
questions.solution: Epiblema is sometimes used in place of the epidermis in root. Thus, the correct sequence from outer to inner side will be epiblema, cortex, endodermis and pericycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The difference between xylem of angiosperms and gymnosperms is that, in gymnosperms
questions.solution: Gymnosperms are non-flowering, seed-bearing plants. Vascular bundles are present in the Gymnosperms but vessels are absent in the xylem and the phloem lacks the companion cells. Presence of vessels in xylem makes is more efficient conducting system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
______ is a couple of layers thick, made of narrow, thin walled and nearly rectangular cells. It cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into __________ or __________ while the inner differentiate into _________ or ____________. The three together is called ____________.

Select the right sequence of words to complete the above.
options: Phellogen, cork, phellem, secondary cortex, phelloderm, periderm
Phellem, phelloderm, cork, secondary cortex, phellogen, periderm
Phellogen, cork, periderm, secondary cortex, phellem, phellem
Phellem, secondary cortex, periderm, cork, phellogen, phelloderm
questions.solution: Phellogen is thick with a couple of layers. It is made of narrow, thin-welled and nearly rectangular cells. Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem, whereas the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm. The cork is impervious to water due to suberin deposition in the cell wall. The cells of the secondary cortex are parenchymatous. Phellogen, phellem and phelloderm are collectively known as periderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Passage cells are thin walled cells found in
options: Phloem elements that serve as entry points for substance for transport to other plant parts
Testa of seeds to enable the emergence of growing embryonic axis during seed germination
The central region of style through which the pollen tube grows towards the ovary
Endodermis of roots facilitating rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle
questions.solution: The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped parenchyma cells without any intercellular spaces. In roots, thick-walled endodermal cells are interrupted by thin-walled passage cells or transfusion tissue. Passage cells facilitate the transportation of water from cortex to pericycle.& The passage cells are thin-walled and are usually located opposite the protoxylem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Provascular tissue gives rise to
questions.solution: Procambium is primary meristematic tissue which undergoes division to form primary vascular tissue such as primary xylem and primary phloem. Secondary xylem and secondary phloem are formed during secondary growth from vascular cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following three statements (A–C) and select the option which includes all the correct ones only:

i. During the primary growth of the plant, specific regions of the apical meristem produce dermal tissue, ground tissue and vascular tissue.
ii. In plants, growth is restricted to specialized regions of active cell division
iii. Secondary meristems are also known as cylindrical meristems.
questions.solution: Plants cells have cells that are totipotent called meristem cells. Apical meristem of root and shoot gives rise to three meristems, first protoderm meristem that gives rise to epidermis, second ground meristem that produces the future cortex and endodermis and third procambium meristem that gives rise to primary vascular tissue and vascular cambium. Cylindrical meristem or secondary meristem increases the width of the cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A mature sieve tube differs from a vessel in
questions.solution: A mature sieve tube lacks lignified walls. Sieve tube in flowering plants has elongated living cells (sieve-tube elements) of the phloem, the nuclei of which are fragmented and disappeared, and the transverse end walls are pierced by sieve-like groups of pores (sieve& plates). They are the conduits of food (mostly sugar) transport.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the correct sequence of pathway of water through the root tissues:
questions.solution: $Roothair \to Cortex \to Endodermis \to Pericycle \to Xylem$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not the feature of the cells showing meristematic growth?
questions.solution: The cells in the meristematic region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei. Their cell walls are primary in nature, thin and cellulosic with abundant plasmodesmata connections. Because of their high metabolic activity, they require more energy so the respiration rate is also very high in them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements about monocot root. Which amongst them are correct?

I. It shows a polyarch condition of xylem.
II. Central pith is less or absent.
III. The monocot root does not undergo secondary growth.
questions.solution: The monocot root is very similar to the dicot root in many aspects with minor similarities. It shows the presence of more than six xylem bundles hence said to have a polyarch condition. The pith is large and prominent. Secondary growth is not seen in monocot root due to the absence of vascular cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Companion cells are present in the phloem of
questions.solution: Companion cell is a type of cell found within the phloem of flowering plants. Each companion cell is usually closely associated with a sieve element. Its function is uncertain, though it appears to regulate the activity of the adjacent sieve element and to take part in loading and unloading sugar into the sieve element.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vessels differ from tracheids in having
options: Presence of perforation plates at both ends
questions.solution: Tracheids are elongated cells in the xylem of vascular plants that serve in the transport of water and mineral salts. Tracheids are one of two types of tracheary elements, vessel elements being the other. Tracheids, unlike vessel elements, do not have perforation plates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the below four layers in proper order starting from the outermost to the innermost layer after secondary growth has already occurred in a dicot stem:

I. Phellem
II. Wood
III. Phelloderm
IV. Vascular cambium
questions.solution: The meristematic tissue called cork cambium or phellogen develops, usually in the cortex region. Phellogen is a couple of layers thick. It is made of narrow, thin-walled, and nearly rectangular cells. Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm. Internal to the secondary cortex lies the xylem (wood), then the vascular cambium and then the phloem is the innermost.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Collenchyma shows all of the following characteristic features, except
options: They possess vacuoles for storage of food
They have cell wall which contains cellulose, pectin and hemicellulose
questions.solution: The collenchyma cells are polygonal or oval in shape. They have thickenings of pectin in the cell wall along with cellulose and hemicellulose. The collenchyma cells are found in the hypodermal layer of the dicot tissues. These cells have negligible intercellular spaces due to pectin deposition. Collenchyma is said to be the living mechanical tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements A and B, each with one or two blanks. Select the option, which correctly fills up the blanks in two statements.

Statements:

(A)& Cicer root is.......(i)........ and......(ii).......
(B) Pith is well developed in the Dicotyledonae stem and.....(i)......
&
options:
(A) (i) Triarch
(ii) Endarch
(B) (i) Monocot root

(A) (i) Monarch
(ii) Mesarch
(B) (i) dicot root
&

(A) (i) Tetrarch
(ii) Exarch
(B) (i) Monocot root

(A) (i) Monarch
(ii) Exarch
(B) (i) Dicot root
questions.solution: In roots, protoxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem towards the center. This condition of the vascular bundle is called exarch; hence,& cicer root has exarch condition.& A well-developed pith is found in monocot root and dicot stem.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following structures is well-developed in hydrophytes?
questions.solution: The cortex of hydrophytes is well developed. Major portion of it is occupied by well-developed prominent air cavity called aerenchyma, which increases buoyancy and allows a rapid gaseous exchange.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Meristems may be classified on the basis of
questions.solution: A meristem is a tissue in plants made of dividing cells. It consists of undifferentiated cells that are capable of cell division and they can develop into all the other tissues and organs that occur in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a dorsiventral leaf, protoxylem is situated towards the (I) surface and protophloem towards the (II) surface in the vascular bundle.
questions.solution: In dorsiventral leaves, protoxylem is situated towards the upper surface (adaxial surface) and protophloem towards the lower surface (abaxial surface) in the vascular bundle. The adaxial surface is the upper surface of the leaf, whereas the abaxial surface is the lower surface.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is true about cuticle in plants?
options: It is always associated with epidermal cells.
It is always associated with ground tissue.
questions.solution: The plant cuticle is an extracellular layer observed over the epidermis of leaves and young shoots of the aerial parts of plants. Its function is to provide protection against desiccation and external environmental stresses. It is secreted by the epidermal tissues having a mix of lipids and hydrocarbon polymers with wax. Cuticle is not synthesized by ground tissue and it is not observed in the root system of the plants but in the aerial parts of the plant body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Given figure is a transverse section of dicot stem showing secondary growth in stelar and extra stelar region. Select the correct option for the parts labelled as a, b, c & d are respectively.
options: Phellem, Phellogen, Primary xylem and Secondary xylem
Secondary xylem, Secondary phloem, Phellogen and Phellem
Primary xylem, Secondary phloem, Phelloederm, phellem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A typical monocotyledonous root is characterized by ___________.
options: usually more than six xylem bundles.
questions.solution:
Monocotyledonous plants are subgroup of Angiosperms characterized by having one embryonic leaf or one cotyledon in their seed. Anatomically the root system of monocots has certain distinguishing feature even though it is similar to that of dicot plant root system.

The root lacks cambium in it and has no secondary growth. The number of xylem bundles are more than dicot, having higher than six. The pith region of monocots is larger in size and better developed than dicots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following tissue systems constitute bulk of the plant body?
questions.solution:
The outermost covering of the whole plant body forms the epidermal tissue system that includes the epidermal cells and appendages with stomata. This system basically provides protection to the main plant body.

Vascular tissue system is made of complex tissues having more than one type of cells working together as one unit. Main function of the unit is transport.

All the tissues excluding epidermal and vascular come in the category of ground tissue system that forms the bulk of the plant body. Simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma form part of the ground tissue system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding the anatomy of a typical monocotyledonous stem
options: Vascular bundles are scattered, conjoint, collateral and closed.
Each vascular bundle is surrounded by a bundle sheath.
Ground tissue is differentiated into cortex, endodermis, pericycle and pith.
questions.solution:
Monocotyledons are the plant group of Angiosperms that have one embryonic leaf (cotyledon) in their seed.

The stem of monocot is quite different from that of a dicot. The stem has no cambium, as a result, secondary growth is absent. The vascular bundles in it are scattered unlike in dicot. They are also conjoint, collateral, and closed. The hypodermis of monocot stem is made of sclerenchymatous tissue and the vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath of the same tissue. In it, phloem parenchyma is absent. Ground tissue is mainly parenchymatous and not differentiated into cortex, pericycle, and pith as the vascular bundles are scattered in it.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: In an old trunk, increase in thickness occurs due to secondary growth, secondary growth in stellar region occurs due to activity of vascular cambium which forms more amount of secondary xylem and this form heart of the trunk.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution:
A large number of rounded, parenchymatous cells with large intercellular spaces which occupy the central portion of the stem constitute the pith of a dicot stem.&

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: The pericycle is cylindrical tissue made up of Parenchyma or sclerenchyma cells, pericycle is present between endodermis and stele. Protoderm is the initial meristematic tissue which forms plumule and radicle. Procambium tissue forms cambium and primary vascular tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In monocots grafting is almost impossible because they lack
questions.solution: Grafting is an artificial propagation technique where two different plants are grafted together. One plant's rooted stock is joined with the non-rooted stem of the other plant (scion). The cambium content must be compatible with this process to get a successful graft. The two parts of the plant grow and develop completely without any mixing or hybridization. For such a process presence of cambium is a must to join the grafts, which is absent in the monocot plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The elongated or tube-like cells, with thick, lignified walls and tapering ends are&
questions.solution:
Xylem is made up of four different kinds of elements in which tracheids are oldest, elongated with thick-walled structures. Tracheids are the main xylem elements in a gymnosperm.

4 types of xylem elements are -

$1.$ Tracheids: Elongated cells with tapering ends. Dead cells (no protoplasm) with lignified cell walls.

$2.$ Vessels (Tracheae): Vessel is tubular structure made up of cells (vessel members) joined together end to end. Dead cells (no protoplasm) with lignified cell walls and a large central cavity. Members are interconnected by their perforated end walls. These are characteristic features of angiosperms (gymnosperms lack vessels).

$3.$ Xylem fibers: Elongated cells with tapering ends and obliterated lumen. Dead cells (no protoplasm) with lignified cell walls. These may be septate or aseptate.

$4.$ Xylem parenchyma: Living cells with a thin cell wall made up of cellulose. These store food (starch, oil), tannin, etc. Ray parenchymatous cells also perform radial conduction of water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant part that possesses polyarch condition of vascular bundles with a well-developed pith is
questions.solution: Dicot root possesses diarch to hexarch (2-6) vascular bundles. Vascular bundle refers to the xylem and phloem tissue which help in water and organic matter transport in different parts of plant. Dicot root has smaller pith and well-developed cambium tissue for secondary growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which among the structure has an elongated, unbranched, pointed, and needle-like apices?
questions.solution:
Phloem fibers are the dead, unbranched structures with needle-like apices. The cell wall is quite thick, without protoplasm. They are also known as Bast fibers. Phloem fibers of jute, flax, and hemp are used commercially.

questions.q: Which tissue is not correctly related to its fate during the secondary growth?
options:

Primary phloem Produced in low amount

Tissue Fate during secondary growth
Cambial ring Cut off secondary permanent tissue on both side

Secondary phloem Synthesized on outer side
questions.solution:
Mechanism in secondary growth in vascular region of dicot stem

$1.$ Vascular cambium (intrafscicular cambium) alongwith interfascicular cambium forms a continuous ring of cambium.

$2.$ Cambial ring becomes active and cut off secondary phloem towards outer side and secondary xylem towards inner side.

$3.$ Secondary xylem is produced more in quantity as cambium is more active in its inner part.

$4.$ When secondary growth repeats few more times, high amount of secondary xylem is accumulates which results in crushing of the primary phloem and most of the secondary phloem (although primary xylem may remain intact).

$5.$ Cambium forms narrow bands of secondary phloem at some places which are termed as medullary rays.

$6.$ Girth of plant increases.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The meristem that occurs in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axis and appear later than primary meristem, is called

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following characteristics (I-V) and identify the structure to which these features correspond.

questions.subject: Botany

In dicot stems, endodermis is also referred as starch sheath
Bark refers to all the tissues outside of the vascular cambium and is a non-technical term.

questions.solution: In dicot root secondary growth in stellar region occurs due to form of vascular cambium which develops from parenchyma cells of pericycle and parenchyma cells of conjuctive tissue to form a complete wavy ring of cambium which is completely secondary in origin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lateral roots and vascular cambium originates due to the activity of which tissue in dicot root?
questions.solution: In dicot root, lateral root originates endogenously due to the activity of cells of pericycle, which undergoes dedifferentiation and becomes meristematic. During secondary growth cells of pericycle and the parenchyma cells of conjuctive tissue becomes meristematic and forms vascular cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pith is absent in
questions.solution: In Monocot stem ground tissue is undifferentiated, it consists of cortex in which vascular bundles are scattered, thus pith is absent. Distinct pith is present in Dicot stem, Dicot root and monocot root, though pith of dicot root is small as compared to monocot root.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Radial vascular bundles characteristically occur in
questions.solution: According to the arrangement of xylem and phloem, they are of 3 basic types of vascular tissues- radial vascular strand, concentric vascular strand and conjoint vascular strand. Radial vascular strand is found in all monocot and dicot roots while concentric vascular bundle is found in stem of fern and yucca whereas conjoint vascular bundle is found in T.S of monocot and dicot stem. Monocot and dicot leaves show collateral close vascular bundle (a type of conjoint vascular bundle).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large empty colourless cells. These cells are called
questions.solution: In grasses and some other monocots cetain adaxial cells becomes large and colourless known as bulliform cells. When these cells absorbs water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed and when they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inward to minimize water loss.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vascular bundle is enclosed within a well developed sclerenchymatous sheath in ________.
questions.solution: There are four tissue systems present in the monocot stem i.e.dermal tissues system, hypodermal tissue system, ground tissue system, and vascular tissue system. The organization of elements of Xylem and phloem in a group is called the vascular bundle. It is found scattered in monocot stems. Its vascular bundle is covered by sclerenchymatous fiber from outside so the fibrovascular bundle is found in monocot stem whereas the sclerenchymatous sheath is not present in the roots.

In dicot stem endodermis is referred as starch sheath

metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ

questions.q: Which of the following types of vascular bundles are found in a monocot root?
options: Radial vascular bundle with exarch xylem
Radial vascular bundle with endarch xylem
questions.solution: In roots vascular bundles are radial in which xylem bundle alternates with phloem bundle and number of xylem bundle is equal to number of phloem bundle. Xylem is exarch in which protoxylem is present towards the periphery and metaxylem is present towards the center.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a mature dicot stem which has undergone secondary growth, the youngest layer of secondary xylem is situated ________________.
options: in between pith and primary xylem
just inner to the vascular cambium
questions.solution: Dicot plants are sub group of the division Angiosperms which have two cotyledons or embryonic leaves in their seeds. Meristematic tissue occurring between the mature regions of root and shoots of angiosperms are called secondary meristem. These generally form by dedifferentiation of the permanent tissues. The vascular cambium tissues found within the vascular tissues like xylem and phloem are secondary meristem which help in lateral growth of the plant helping in increasing the girth of the stem. The cambium cells between the xylem and phloem is called as intra fascicular cambium. The new cambium cells that form towards the pith and mature into secondary xylem that is inner to the vascular cambium and the cells forming towards the periphery on the outer side is called secondary phloem. The younger cambium cells that will develop into xylem grow towards the central or inner side of the stem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Collenchyma constitutes the hypodermis in
questions.solution:
Collenchyma, part of the ground tissue, is a simple living tissue found in plants. Collenchyma layer is generally found below epidermis of the plant. They are either found in a patch manner or even distributed throughout. The cell wall of collenchyma tissue cells is thickened at corner due to higher deposition of cellulose, pectin and hemicellulose. The cells are generally spherical or polygonal in shape. This tissue provides mechanical support to the young stem and leaf.

The cross section of dicot plant stem has epidermis as the outermost layer and the region between pericycle and epidermis is called the cortex. The cortex of the stem is sub-divided in to regions and the section nearest to the epidermis is called hypodermis. The hypodermis (below epidermis) layer in dicot stem is made of collenchyma tissues compactly arranged. Whereas in the monocot stem, the hypodermis is made of sclerenchyma tissue.

questions.solution:
Collenchyma, part of the ground tissue, is a simple living tissue found in plants. The cell wall of collenchyma tissue cells is thickened at corner due to higher deposition of cellulose, pectin and hemicellulose. The cells are generally spherical or polygonal in shape. This tissue provides mechanical support to the young stem and leaf. The outermost covering of the whole plant body forms the epidermal tissue system that includes the epidermal cells and appendages with stomata. This system basically provides protection to the main plant body. The outermost layer of primary plant body called as epidermis have elongated compactly arranged cells. Stomata structures present in the epidermis help in regulating transpiration and gas exchange. These stomata are made of two guard cells each that encloses the pore.

Meristem are a type of tissue found in such plants which can divide indefinitely. These are generally considered undifferentiated as they can give develop into all other tissues and organs of the plant. The meristematic tissues that appear early in plant life and help in formation of the plant body is called primary meristem. The apical and intercalary meristem are included in it. Meristematic tissue occurring between the mature regions of root and shoots of angiosperms are called secondary meristem.

Parenchyma is a type of simple permanent tissues forming a major component of the tissues of plant. These cells are in various shapes like oval, round, polygonal etc. with a thin cell wall made of cellulose. These cells perform functions like storage, photosynthesis, secretion.

The simple permanent tissue consisting of dead cells without protoplast is called sclerenchyma. These cells are long and narrow with lignified cell wall. The thick-walled, elongated pointed cells form the sclerenchyma fibres and the spherical, oval shaped cell with highly thickened cell wall and narrow cavity form the sclerenchyma sclereids.

Epidermal cells found around the guard cells are called subsidiary cells. The cells are also referred to as accessory cells.

The simple permanent tissue consisting of dead cells without protoplast is called sclerenchyma. These cells are long and narrow with lignified cell wall. Conjoint further subdivided into collateral, bicollateral, and concentric.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vascular cambium and cork cambium are the examples of ______.
questions.solution: Growth in the plant is of two types i.e.primary and secondary growth. Primary growth mainly occurs in the primary meristem. They help in increasing the length of the plant because they present on the axis of it. On the lateral side of it, axillary buds are present that form branches. Secondary meristem is of two types i.e. vascular cambium and cork cambium. Vascular cambium is present in between vascular tissue that helps in the secondary growth of the plants and increases the girth of the plants by the addition of cells in the lateral direction. Similarly, cork cambium also helps in the addition of cells in the cortex. So the correct answer is $B$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding meristematic cells and select the CORRECT ones

(i) Root apical meristem occupies the tip of the root while the shoot apical meristem occupies the distant most region of the stem axis.
(ii)& The meristem which occurs between mature tissues is known as intercalary meristem.
(iii) Both apical meristems and intercalary meristems are secondary meristems.
questions.solution: The meristems which occur at the tips of roots and shoots and produce primary tissues are called apical meristems.& Root apical meristem occupies the tip of a root while the shoot apical meristem occupies the distant most region of the stem axis. During the formation of leaves and elongation of stem, some cells ‘left behind’ from shoot apical meristem, constitute the axillary bud. Such buds are present in the axils of leaves and are capable of forming a branch or a flower. The meristem which occurs between mature tissues is known as intercalary meristem. They occur in grasses and regenerate parts removed by the grazing herbivores. Both apical meristems and intercalary meristems are primary meristems because they appear early in life of a plant and contribute to the formation of the primary plant body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A common structural feature of vessel elements and sieve tube elements is ________.
questions.solution: The food conducting tissue of vascular plants is phloem. The components of phloem are sieve elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, phloem fibers, and sclereids. Whereas xylem is the water-conducting tissue of vascular plants. The components of xylem are Tracheids, vessel, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fiber. There is one characteristic that is common in vessel element and sieve tube element is that they both are non-living at maturity or nucleus is absent in both of them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In dicot stem, vascular bundles are:
questions.solution:
The characteristic features of vascular bundles of dicot stem are as follows:
1. Vascular bundles are arranged in a ring.
2. They are conjoint, i.e. xylem and phloem are present on the same radius.
3. They are open, i.e. cambium layer is found between xylem and phloem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
questions.solution: Collenchyma is living mechanical tissue. Phellem or cork is made up of dead cell and its cell wall is deposited with suberin which makes it impermeable. Sieve tube elements are long, tube-like structures, arranged longitudinally and are associated with the companion cells. Their end walls are perforated in a sieve-like manner to form the sieve plates. A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus. The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the nucleus of companion cells. Xylem parenchyma are living parenchyma cells associated with xylem to store water and minerals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following is generally present in dicot stem but absent in monocot stem?

(i) Endodermis (ii) Pericycle (iii) Medullary ray (iv) Phloem parenchyma (v) Pith (vi) Epidermis
questions.solution: In dicot stem, ground tissue is well-differentiated and consists of endodermis, pericycle, medullary rays and the central part as pith. In monocot, ground tissue is undifferentiated and lacks endodermis, pericycle, medullary rays and the central part as pith. Phloem parenchyma is absent in monocot stem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In plants towards the centre of the root, next to endodermis lies a few layers of thick-walled parenchymatous cells referred to as
questions.solution:
In the root of angiospermic plant, the tissue group adjacent to endodermis and towards the central part is called as pericycle. Pericycle generally is composed of parenchymatous cell and in the centre of it lies the pith which is mostly inconspicuous. Formation of lateral root and vascular cambium during the secondary growth occurs at this section.

Epidermis forms the outermost layer of the root having cells giving out root hair in some cells. Phloem is a type of complex vascular tissue which helps in transportation of food throughout the plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lysigenous cavity in monocot stems vascular bundles developed by the dissolution of _________.
questions.solution: There are four tissue systems present in monocot stems i.e. dermal tissue system, hypodermal tissue system, ground tissue system, and vascular bundle system. There are barrel-shaped parenchymatous cells found in the epidermis. Trichomes are absent in the monocot stem and below the epidermis, there is a layer of the hypodermal cell present. The ground tissue is undifferentiated in monocot stem which is made up of loosely arranged parenchyma cells. There is a vascular bundle which is found scattered in the ground tissue. Xylem is found on the inner side whereas phloem on the outer side and cambium is absent in monocot stem. So, the inner protoxylem is non-functional and remains water-filled. This water-filled cavity is called the lysigenous cavity or protoxylem cavity.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which out of the following is a MISMATCHED pair?
options: Hypostomatic - Stomata present more on lower epidermis than on upper epidermis
Epistomatic - Stomata present more on upper epidermis than on lower epidermis
Sunken stomata - Stomata deep seated below the surface
questions.solution: Stomata are pore in a plant's leaf through which water and gases are exchanged with the atmosphere. Stomata consist of three parts i.e., cell pore, guard cells, and subsidiary cells. Guard cells are specialized cells that surround cell pore and helps the stomata in opening and closing. There are some epidermal cells present around the guard cells that are known as subsidiary cells. On the basis of the position of stomata, they are of the following types i.e. hypostomatic, epistomatic, amphistomatic, and sunken stomata. In amphistomatic, the stomata are present on both sides of the leaf.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement from the following about the anatomy of angiosperms.
options: The cells of medullary rays, adjoining the intrafascicular cambium becomes meristematic and forms interfascicular cambium.
In isobilateral leaf, the mesophyll is undifferentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
Vascular bundles in a dicot stem are arranged in a scattered manner.
Bulliform cells are observed in the leaves of some monocots.
questions.solution: Vascular bundles in dicot stem are conjoint, collateral and open, they are arranged in ring around the central pith. Scattered vascular bundles are present in monocot stem in which ground tissue is undifferentiated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sclereids are present in
questions.solution: Sclereids are spherical, oval, cylindrical cells with a very narrow lumen in sclerenchyma. That is also known as stone cells. Sclereids possess a very thick and hard cell wall. It is found in fruit walls of nuts, the pulp of fruits like guava and pear, seed coats of legumes, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In endarch condition of xylem, metaxylem lies _____ of protoxylem
options: both on inner and outer side
questions.solution: The endarch condition of xylem refers to the condition when the metaxylem lies towards the periphery and the protoxylem towards the pith while in exarch condition the metaxylem lies towards the centre and the protoxylem is situated towards the periphery. Endarch condition is seen in stem whereas exarch condition is found in roots of all vascular plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All of the following are lateral meristem, except
questions.solution: The meristem which occurs between mature tissue is known as intercalary meristem. They occur in grasses and regenerate parts removed by the grazing herbivores. It is primary meristem and contributes to the formation of primary plant body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Stele includes all of these except
questions.solution: The central part present in the root or stem having the tissues derived from the procambium is known as stele in plants. The stele contains the vascular bundles, xylem and phloem for the storage and transport of water and nutrients. Pith is a ground tissue which stores and transports nutrients in the plants and is located in the centre of the stem in some plants. The pericycle is a layer of cells which surrounds the stele.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the CORRECT ones

(i) Phloem parenchyma is absent in most monocots.
(ii) Gymnosperms lack tracheids and vessels.
(iii) Gymnosperms lack companion cells.
questions.solution:
In Angiosperms phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres. Food material and other substances (Resin, mucilage and latex) are stored in phloem parenchyma. Phloem parenchyma is absent in monocots. Sieve tubes and companion cells are absent in Gymnosperms. Albuminous cells and sieve cells are present in gymnosperms.

Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres. Vessels are absent in gymnosperms but elongated and tube like tracheids are present.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of meristematic cells?
questions.solution: The cells residing at the root and shoot tips are known as meristem cells. These are undifferentiated cells and are responsible for the plant growth due to its ability to divide. These cells are small and have thin cellulosic cell walls with large nuclei, small or absent vacuoles, and absence of intercellular spaces. These cells also help to increase the length of the plant as well as the girth (lateral growth) of the stem, branches and roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following parts of the plant is used as commercial wood?
questions.solution: Wood is a porous and fibrous structural tissue found in the stems and roots of trees and other woody plants. It is an organic material - a natural composite of cellulose fibers that are strong in tension and embedded in a matrix of lignin that resists compression, this is the product of old secondary xylem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The following figure corresponds to:

&
questions.solution: The regions in plants which undergo active cell division are known as meristems. The parenchyma, sclerenchyma and collenchymas are simple tissues, where the parenchyma is majorly found within organs. The collenchyma is found in patches or homogenous layers in layers below the epidermis in dicot plants and the sclerenchyma tissue consists of narrow cells with thick walls usually spherical, oval or cylindrical with narrow cavities.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a dicot leaf, palisade tissue is generally present adjacent to the epidermis
questions.solution: The palisade cells are found in the mesophyll which is situated between the upper and the lower epidermis and is made up of parenchyma. The palisade parenchyma is made up of thin-walled elongated cells which lie vertically and are parallel to each other. This tissue is located below the adaxial epidermis(the upper epidermis having stomata) or adjacent to the abaxial epidermis(lower epidermis not having stomata).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The certain endodermal cell which is present opposite to the xylem bundle remain thin-walled, these cells are
questions.solution: The cell wall of endodermis is deposited with suberin in the form of strips known as Casparin strips, which makes the layer impermeable. Few cells of endodermis lying opposite to the protoxylem lack suberin on their tangential wall, these are called passage cells which maintains the unidirectional flow of water from outsite to inside.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following and choose the correct option from the below table.
&
& Column-I & Column-II
[A] Meristem (i) Photosynthesis, storage
[B] Parenchyma (ii) Mechanical support
[C] Collenchyma (iii) Actively dividing cells
[D] Sclerenchyma (iv) Stomata
[E] Epidermal tissue (v) Sclereids
questions.solution: Meristem are actively dividing cells present at root apex and shoot apex. Parenchyma are living photosynthetic tissue which also carries out storage of food. Collenchyma are living mechanical tissue. Sclerenchyma consists of elongated cells called as fibers and small round cells called as sclereids. Epidermal cells are modified to form stomata for transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Jute fibres are obtained from the:
questions.solution: Jute fibers are bast fibers or phloem fibers. Secondary phloem forms the fibre which are long and are commercially important. Other fibers like flax and hemp are also phloem fibers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement from the following.
options: In spring season cambium is more active and produces a large quantity of xylem having vessels with wider lumen.
The spring wood is also known as early wood.
In winter, the cambium is less active and forms less xylem elements having narrow vessels this is called autumn wood or late wood.
The spring wood is dark in colour and has lower density.
questions.solution: In spring season cambium is more active and produces large quantity of xylem having vessels with wider lumen.& The wood formed during this season is called spring wood or early wood. In winter, the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels, and this wood is called autumn wood or late wood. The spring wood is lighter in colour and has a lower density whereas the autumn wood is darker and has a higher density.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: In the dicot root, the vascular cambium is completely secondary in origin.
Wood is the common name used for secondary xylem.
A mature sieve tube element lacks peripheral cytoplasm, a large vacuole and a prominent nucleus.
Lenticels are the aerating pores present in the bark of plants and are associated with gaseous exchange.
questions.solution: A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus. The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the nucleus of companion cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All of the following statements are incorrect about a monocot stem, except
options: hypodermis of monocot stem is made up of multiple layers of parenchyma
vascular bundles are surrounded by sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.
the vascular cylinder is surrounded by a parenchymatous pericycle in monocot stem
peripheral vascular bundles are generally larger than the centrally located ones.
questions.solution: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. It doesn't have pericycle. Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed. Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In an annual ring, the light coloured part is known as:
questions.solution: Annual ring consists of two concentric light and dark colour ring, which are formed due unequal activity of cambium in different season. In spring season the cambium is more active producing more amount of secondary xylem with wider lumen which is light in colour, in autumn season cambium is less active and produces less amount of xylem with narrow lumen and which is dark in colour.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Epidermal tissue system is derived from
questions.solution: Protoderm is referred to as the meristem in vascular plants that gives rise to the epidermis. The epidermal tissue provides protection against infection, water loss, and any mechanical injuries. This protective tissue is derived from the protoderm (primary meristem). The protoderm is also known as dermatogens and consists of the epidermis as well as epidermal outgrowths.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In temperate regions, cambium is less active during the winter season and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels, this wood is called ____________.
questions.solution:
In the spring season, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities. The wood formed during this season is called spring wood or early wood. In winter, the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels, and this wood is called autumn wood or late wood.

In old trees, the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown due to deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils in the central or innermost layers of the stem. These substances make it hard, durable and resistant to the attacks of microorganisms and insects. This region comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls and is called heartwood. The peripheral region of the secondary xylem, is lighter in colour and is known as the sapwood.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In grasses, bulliform cells are
options: large bubble-shaped epidermal cells, present on the lower surface of leaves
large bubble-shaped epidermal cells, present on the upper surface of leaves
small pyramidal epidermal cells, present on the upper surface of leaves
small pyramidal epidermal cells, present on the lower surface of leaves
questions.solution: Bulliform cells spread around the leaf on the upper surface play a role for water storage. These cells assist during transpiration process to reduce water loss. During stress, these cells lose water causing the leaves to curl and prevent damage. They are commonly found in the grasses.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Find the correct option:
&
& Column: A & Column: B
$( A )$ Parenchyma $1 . Living tissue that provides mechanical support
\left(B\right) Collenchyma $2 . Food storage
$\left(C\right)$ Sclerenchyma 3 . Dead& tissue that provides mechanical support
questions.solution: Parenchyma function is the storage of food, photosynthesis and secretion. Collenchyma is a living tissue whose main function is mechanical support and photosynthesis also. Sclerenchyma is a dead tissue whose main function is mechanical support.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In old trees, the central dark-coloured, non-conducting part of secondary xylem is referred to
questions.solution: Over time the centre of the innermost layers of the stem gets deposited with organic compounds like tannins, raisins, oils, gums and other aromatic substances. This deposition gives the secondary xylem a dark brownish colour and makes it durable and resistant to the microorganisms and insects. This dead inner wood with highly lignified walls is known as the hardwood. They are not involved in the conduction and transport of water but gives mechanical support to the stem. The sapwood is the outermost portion of the secondary xylem lighter in colour and involved in the conduction of water and minerals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The meristem that occurs in the mature regions of root and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axis and appear later than primary meristem is called
questions.solution: The meristematic cell present on mature root and shoot which produce a woody axis known as lateral meristem. They are cylindrical meristem and are the secondary meristems that induce the growth of the plant with increasing girth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The periderm is produced by:
questions.solution: A periderm is a group of cylindrical tissues that forms a protective layer and cover the stems and roots of many plants during the secondary growth. These tissues are usually found in perennial plants and consist of three different layers, the phelloderm (inner surface of the cork cambium), the phellogen (meristematic tissue called the cork cambium) which gives rise to the periderm and the phellem which is the suberized cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following cells is usually dead and without a protoplasm?
questions.solution: It is long,narrow cells with thick and lignified cell wall having a pits. They are usually dead and without protoplasts. They provides mechanical support to organ.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pith and cortex do not differentiate in
questions.solution: In a monocot stem, the pith and cortex do not get bifurcated. Vascular bundles are many in number and are scattered. The ground meristem comprises of only hypodermis and ground parenchyma.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Living mechanical tissue is
questions.solution: The collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants. Deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectin. It provide tensile strength.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In temperate regions, during the spring season, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities; wood formed in this way is called ______.
questions.solution: The environmental and physiological factors influence the cambium activity, due to which the climatic conditions in the temperate regions which are not uniform results in the cambium changes. In the spring season, the cambium activity increases to a great extent and a large number of xylary elements are produced, having vessels with wider cavities and the name given to this wood is the springwood or earlywood. During winters, the cambium becomes less active and the xylem vessels formed have a narrow cavity known as the autumn wood or the latewood.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the correct option regarding the wall of parenchyma.

A. Thick
B. Made of pectin
C. Thin
D. Made of cellulose
questions.solution: Parenchyma forms the major component within organs. The cells of the parenchyma are generally isodiametric. They may be spherical, oval, round, polygonal or elongated in shape. Their walls are thin and made up of cellulose.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cork is commonly used for sealing bottles. It is produced by
questions.solution: Cork cambium or phellogen is a type of cambium arising within the outer layer of the stems of woody plants, usually as a complete ring surrounding the inner tissues. The cells of the cork cambium divide to produce an outer corky tissue (cork or phellem) and an innerly secondary cortex (phelloderm). The common bottle cork produced from Quercus suber is a product of phellogen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The chief water-conducting elements of xylem in Sequoia tree are
questions.solution: The chief water-conducting element of xylem in gymnosperms are called tracheids. These are elongated cells with tapering ends and are dead because of the deposition of lignin. These show scalariform, annular, reticulate, or bordered pitted thickening. These are the only water-conducting xylem elements in both gymnosperms and pteridophytes. Generally, vessels are absent in gymnosperms with exceptions like Gnetum, Welwitschia, Ephedra, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following meristems are completely secondary in origin ?

A. Cork cambium of a dicot stem
B. Vascular cambium of a dicot stem
C. Cork cambium of a dicot root
D. Vascular cambium of a dicot root
questions.solution:
Interfascicular Cambium:

A. This cambium is secondary meristem.
B. It develops from the parenchymatous cells of medullary rays.
C. It is located between two consecutive vascular bundles.
D. During secondary growth its derivatives are secondary phloem, secondary xylem and conjunctive tissue.

Intrafascicular Cambium:

A. It is primary meristem.
B. It develops from the procambium of the stem apex.
C. It is located inside the open vascular bundles, between phloem and xylem patches.
D. During secondary growth the derivatives are only secondary phloem and secondary xylem.

Vascular cambium of a dicot stem, Cork cambium of a dicot root and Vascular cambium of a dicot root are completely secondary in origin. In stem only Interfasciculated cambium is secondary in origin. Dicot stem have Intrafascicular Cambium which is primary meristem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a lateral meristem?
questions.solution: Lateral meristems, intercalary meristems, and apical meristems are the three types of meristems that are present in the plants. The vascular cambium present on the lateral sides are the lateral meristems and they are the intrafascicular cambium and interfascicular cambium. Phellogen is the cork cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bidirectional translocation of solutes takes place in:
questions.solution: Sugars produced in sources, such as leaves, need to be delivered to growing parts of the plant via the phloem in a process called translocation, or movement of sugar. The points of sugar delivery, such as roots, young shoots, and developing seeds, are called sinks. It is done by phloem tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Observe the following diagram and select the property that is false.
options: It provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as young stem and petiole of leaves.
It is present below the epidermis in the form of a homogenous layer or as patches in dicot stem.
It is present in the form of semilunar patches in the pericycle of monocot stem.
questions.solution: The collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in most of the dicotyledonous plants. It is found either as a homogeneous layer or in patches. It consists of cells which are much thickened at the corners due to deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Collenchymatous cells may be oval, spherical or polygonal and often contain chloroplasts. These cells assimilate food when they contain chloroplasts. Intercellular spaces are absent. They provide mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as young stem and petiole of a leaf.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following options CORRECTLY shows the sequence of different tissues of the periderm starting from the periphery?
questions.solution: The cylindrical tissue that forms the protective covering of stems and roots during the early secondary growth of perennial plants is known as periderm. They are seen only in plants that show secondary growth and these tissues replace the epidermis of the same plant. Phellem or the cork is present in the outer cortical cells and prevents the rupturing of the outer tissues. Phellogen is the cork cambium and is found on the side of the phellem. Phelloderm is the secondary cortex which is produced in the inner side of the phellogen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the false statement about parenchyma.
options: The cells of the parenchyma are generally isodiametric.
They are found in both polygonal and elongated shapes.
Their walls are thick and made up of pectin.
The functions of parenchyma include photosynthesis, storage and secretion.
questions.solution: Parenchyma forms the major component within organs. The cells of the parenchyma are generally isodiametric. They may be spherical, oval, round, polygonal or elongated in shape. Their walls are thin and made up of cellulose. They may either be closely packed or have small intercellular spaces. The parenchyma performs various functions like photosynthesis, storage, secretion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about a woody dicot stem which shows extensive secondary growth?
options: The primary xylem persists in the centre of the axis.
Primary and the older secondary phloem get crushed.
Secondary xylem forms the bulk of the stem.
questions.solution: Secondary growth is responsible for thickening the stem and roots, making them woody. This growth is a result of cell division in the cambium. When a woody dicot stem undergoes secondary growth the primary xylem (formed from the procambium) persists inside the stem in the centre of the axis without being damaged or changed during the growth. The secondary xylem is found covering the primary xylem and keeps growing in girth forming the bulk of stem. Due to this growth of the xylem during the secondary growth, the primary phloem and the older secondary phloem they get crushed towards the epidermis and form the wood.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which type of vascular bundle, xylem is covered on both sides by phloem?
questions.solution: A vascular bundle is a long continuous strand of conductive tissues that extend from the roots through the stem and into the leaves. It consists of xylem and phloem that may differ in their arrangement. A vascular bundle having the phloem and cambium strands on both the outer and inner sides of xylem are called bicollateral. The arrangement is in a sequence of outer phloem, outer cambium, xylem, inner cambium, and inner phloem, for example,& Cucurbita.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are secondary medullary rays?
questions.solution: During secondary growth, at some places, the cambium forms a narrow band of parenchyma, which passes through the secondary xylem and the secondary phloem in the radial directions. These are the secondary medullary rays.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following structures based on their location from the periphery to centre with respect to the anatomy of a dicotyledonous root.
I. Pericycle
II.& Casparian strips
III.& Epiblema
IV. Conjunctive tissue
options: IV, I, II, III
IV, II, III,I
I, II, III, IV
III, II, I, IV
questions.solution: The outermost layer is epiblema. Many of the cells of epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells, with intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential, as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells, have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips. Next to endodermis lies a few layers of thick-walled parenchymatous cells referred to as pericycle. Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during the secondary growth takes place in these cells. The pith is small or inconspicuous. The parenchymatous cells which lie between the xylem and the phloem are called conjunctive tissue.
